ctx.x: Later I heard that the reason Django did not show up for the concert was because he happened to meet Marcel Cerdan, the French boxer, and as he was lonesome, he was so happy to be able to speak French that he started drinking with Marcel and forgot about the concert. However, it was said that Django did arrive later, but had no guitar and was not dressed formally for the concert.

We recorded for a new record company called MGM which I think was affiliated with the movie company. This date was with the band and there were numbers where some vocals were done by Sy and Dickie Wells, Henri Wells and the whole orchestra. Sy was keen on the 'Glee Club Style' of singing and knew the technique of it. He had done it with the Lunceford orchestra successfully and on a few numbers with the Dorsey band. After two months at the Zanzibar, we finished in January 1947. As a rule, bands usually stayed in clubs of that standing for months no end and in some cases for years, as Dule Ellington did at the Cotton Club in Harlem. Charlie Johnson at Small's Paradise, Fletcher Henderson at the Roseland Ball room, which was a rare occasion for a dance hall, and numerous other orchestras that stayed in cabarets for six months and sometimes years.
